effects.prompt: Banish a Shadow card from your hand?
Banish a card from the defending hero's soul?

_comment:
Shadow Token - Demon Ally, 6{p}/6{h}. 'Once per Turn Action - 0: Attack' / 'Whenever Blasmophet attacks, you may banish a Shadow card from your hand. If you do, you may banish a card from the defending hero's soul.'

THE FILE HAD TO EXIST AT ALL: create_token calls require_card, so doomsday_blue's token creation raised MissingCardImplementation and aborted the game.

ACTIVATION COST IS DECLARED TOP-LEVEL AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. card.py derives an activation cost by counting {r} in the 'TYPE - COST:' prefix and only accepts a count > 0, so a printed cost of '0' leaves activation_cost None -- and play._add_weapon_attacks refuses to offer an attack whose activation_cost is None. Without the declaration this ally could never attack. loader.compile_card reads raw['activation_cost'] TOP-LEVEL; one nested only inside an ability is silently unread (the same trap raydn_duskbane documents).

THE TWO 'MAY'S NEST because the second is gated on the first: 'if you do' means the soul banish happens only when the hand banish was actually paid. A MAY whose `cost` cannot be paid runs nothing, so an empty hand skips both halves rather than granting the payoff for free.

'A SHADOW CARD' IS A TALENT, not a class. _hand_card_filter's class check read only `c.classes`, so a class_filter of 'Shadow' matched nothing and the cost could never be paid; it now matches classes OR talents (the names are disjoint in FAB) and takes an explicit `talent` key, which is what this file uses.

Defending hero's soul: BANISH's target spec resolves controller 'opponent' + zone SOUL through the shared zone map. The attacking player is this token's controller, so the opponent IS the defending hero in every state this trigger fires in.
